claims.statement: Every held order was routed to the east node and flagged by the overnight allocator as a split-reservation exception (scope EXC-0921); reports began about 06:00 and are ongoing.
claims.corroboration: Now corroborated by a tier-1 verified exception_audit from Inventory Control (the allocation-system owner), a distinct owner from the original tier-2 customer_support report; tier-1 source alone is sufficient for established.
claims.limitation: The audit itself states this cannot separate an effect of the rule change from an effect specific to the east-node lanes, because only rule-affected orders were routed there (100% overlap is confounded, not yet causal).

claims.statement: The stuck cohort (186 orders, scope EXC-0921) is 100% coincident with orders that received a v18 split-reservation exception; no order outside EXC-0921 is held. This is a strong correlation between rule v18's east-node-first reservation logic and the stuck state, but not yet discriminating between an allocation-side defect and an unrelated east-node-specific carrier/dock issue, since only rule-affected orders were ever routed to the east node.
claims.corroboration: Tier-1 exception_audit (m8_r_exceptions) plus tier-1 rule record (m8_e03) and tier-1 monitor alert (m8_e02), all consistent.
claims.limitation: Confounded: cannot yet distinguish 'the split-reservation exception itself blocks pickup handoff' from 'something independent about east-node lanes (carrier feed lag, dock capacity) is the true blocker and the rule change is merely why orders went there'. Needs a diagnostic that traces where in the pipeline the block occurs.

next_action.rationale: m8_r_exceptions explicitly flags a confound: 100% of held orders are in EXC-0921, but only rule-affected orders were ever routed to the east node, so correlation with v18 cannot yet be separated from an unrelated east-node-specific issue (carrier feed lag, dock capacity). Now that the scope EXC-0921 is on record, tracing the cohort's handoffs from allocation through to carrier pickup will show precisely where the pipeline breaks (e.g., the split-reservation exception itself prevents the pickup handoff to the carrier, vs. the handoff completes normally and a separate east-node carrier/dock issue is blocking collection).
next_action.expected_information_gain: Produces discriminating evidence that resolves the confound noted in C7/m8_r_exceptions, needed before any claim can be upgraded to kind=root_cause, and rules in or out carrier_feed_lag/dock_capacity as the true mechanism versus allocation_rule_defect.
